goal: Estimate how coordinated activation of exported Russian-origin DPI/SORM or TSPU-like filtering could affect United States users, services, organizations and network reachability, while separating direct US network impact from indirect international effects.

scenarios.name: LOCAL_FOREIGN_ACTIVATION
scenarios.description: One foreign operator using Russian-origin DPI/SORM activates new filtering, throttling or interception rules.
expected_effects: Users in that country lose or degrade access to selected US cloud, communications, developer, media or financial services.
US companies serving the affected market see support incidents, lower availability and misleading regional telemetry.
US personnel and partners operating locally face increased surveillance and degraded secure communications.
scenarios.best_discriminator: Operator-local packet fingerprint with normal reachability from matched neighboring/control ASes.

scenarios.name: SYNCHRONIZED_MULTI_COUNTRY_ACTIVATION
scenarios.description: Several operators/countries with common Russian-origin DPI/SORM technology introduce similar filtering in a narrow window.
expected_effects: Simultaneous reachability degradation to US-hosted services across multiple foreign markets.
Loss of reliable communications with regional partners, journalists, NGOs, businesses and travelers.
Cloud/CDN providers may reroute traffic or shift protocol behavior, complicating incident attribution.
Economic impact is more likely through customers, payment/communications dependencies and regional operations than through failure of the US domestic Internet.
scenarios.best_discriminator: Shared packet/protocol fingerprint plus common vendor/operator lineage and independent measurement from multiple countries.

scenarios.name: FOREIGN_DPI_PLUS_ROUTE_REDIRECTION
scenarios.description: Traffic that normally avoids filtering infrastructure is redirected through a controlled or compromised AS/path and then filtered, observed or blackholed.
expected_effects: Foreign-origin traffic to US destinations can be intercepted or disrupted even if the endpoint country itself has no Russian equipment.
If US-origin return paths are also redirected, selected bidirectional sessions can fail or leak metadata.
Large providers may experience regional reachability anomalies without a failure in their own application stack.
required_bridge: BGP/AS-path change or other verified routing shift
path localization to the filtering segment
matched bypass route without the effect
scenarios.us_defense_relevance: FCC/CISA routing-security guidance makes RPKI, ROA/ROV, strict route filtering and route-change monitoring the primary defensive controls for this scenario.

scenarios.name: REMOTE_ACCESS_TO_EXPORTED_SURVEILLANCE_STACK
scenarios.description: A Russian vendor or state-linked actor retains or obtains remote administrative access to foreign-deployed interception equipment.
expected_effects: Potential collection of metadata or content transiting the foreign operator subject to encryption and local architecture.
US government, corporate and partner communications in affected countries become a counterintelligence concern.
Availability impact is secondary unless remote access is used to modify filtering/routing policy.
scenarios.claim_limit: Public reporting raises this risk but does not prove Russian government access to any specific deployment.

scenarios.name: MASS_ACTIVATION_PLUS_NETWORK_INTRUSION
scenarios.description: Coordinated filtering activation is combined with compromise of routers, transit providers or routing control planes.
expected_effects: Regional or multi-regional loss of access to US services.
Traffic redirection, interception or blackholing beyond networks that intentionally deployed the filtering stack.
Complex failure signatures that resemble cloud outages, DDoS or ordinary routing incidents.
Potential strategic pressure on communications during a geopolitical crisis.
scenarios.important_boundary: This scenario is no longer 'TSPU activation alone'; it requires a separate cyber/routing operation and must be evidenced independently.

us_exposure_layers.note: Foreign DPI cannot normally control routes that never traverse it. Direct domestic impact requires US-located infrastructure, compromised routing, traffic redirection or a shared upstream dependency.
This is the most realistic first-order US consequence of synchronized foreign filtering: foreign users lose access to US services even though the US service remains healthy.
Surveillance, DNS manipulation and secure-protocol blocking can affect confidentiality and availability of communications in countries using the equipment.
Regional filtering can interrupt operational links, support channels, development infrastructure, payments or telemetry used by US organizations.
Risk becomes materially higher if censorship infrastructure is paired with BGP hijack/leak, compromised transit or policy-based redirection.

defensive_priorities_for_us_validation: Measure reachability to a stable set of US cloud/CDN/SaaS endpoints from countries/operators with known Russian DPI/SORM procurement.
Maintain RIPE Atlas/OONI/control-vantage baselines so activation can be detected as a change rather than inferred after an outage.
Track BGP path and RPKI state for the same measurements to distinguish filtering from route manipulation.
Correlate packet/protocol fingerprints across countries before inferring coordination.
Use provider RCAs and US-side telemetry as negative controls.
Treat synchronized DNS/QUIC/TLS policy changes across common-vendor networks as an early-warning signal, not immediate attribution.
current_conclusion: A mass activation of exported Russian-origin DPI/SORM would most plausibly hurt the United States indirectly first: by cutting foreign users, partners and operations off from US services and by increasing interception risk abroad. A severe direct impact on the US domestic Internet becomes credible only if filtering is paired with route redirection, compromised transit/control planes, or infrastructure physically/logically present on US-relevant paths. That bridge is not currently established and is the highest-value object for TOPA+Spider to monitor.
